set.body:
Prerequisite for every other child of the interactive-rate epic. Today the
performance gate records cardinality, not time, over six workloads
(`performance/baselines/v1.tsv`, `docs/limits.md:29-71`), none of them
faceted, and `performance/README.md:2-5` states it "deliberately does not
fail CI on elapsed time".

Nothing here proposes gating CI on wall clock. The ask is that a cost model
exists at all, so the optimisation children are judged against measurements
rather than against reading the source.

Add workloads that match how consumers actually drive the library:

- `facet-grid-30`: 6 conditions x 5 groups = 30 panels, 20 series each,
  shared scales, `geomLine` + `geomRibbon`. Report per-phase time (mapping,
  stat, scale training, resolve, layout, lowering) so the (panels + 1) pass
  structure in `FacetCompiler.scala:114-121` is visible.
- `facet-grid-sparse`: same shape with half the cross-product cells empty, to
  expose the `facetGrid` full-cross-product cost (`Facet.scala:188-194`).
- `facet-free-scales`: the same plot under `FacetScales.Free`, to price
  per-panel axis lowering and tick measurement
  (`FacetCompiler.scala:220-256`, `:341-352`).
- `resize-only`: compile once, then re-resolve at 5 successive
  `RenderContext` sizes with identical data. This is the workload that should
  approach zero statistical work once the data/device split lands.
- `pick-dense`: `PickingPlan.nearest` over a 20k-mark faceted plot, to price
  the exhaustive scan the interaction README already flags.
- `rich-vs-lean`: the same faceted plot through `PlotBuilder.resolve`
  (`rich`, Full provenance) and `PlotCompiler.compile` (`lean`), since the
  defaults differ (`docs/limits.md:133-134`, `PlotCompiler.scala:80-90`) and
  the point-batch IR only engages in one of them (`docs/limits.md:91-94`).

Deliverable: recorded elapsed time and allocation per workload per phase, on
named hardware, plus a short note in `docs/limits.md` replacing "we publish
no throughput numbers" with what is now known. Report ranges and run counts;
do not present a single run as a benchmark.
set.title: Measure first: add faceted and resize-only workloads to the performance baseline
